answer: The official OpenAI Python SDK’s stable channel is the 1.x line of the "openai" package. Releases are frequent—typically several times per month, often weekly to biweekly—though exact timing varies with development activity. If you need the freshest version, check the PyPI release history or the GitHub Releases page.

findings.detail: PyPI shows the package on the 1.x series as the current stable line, with new 1.x point releases published regularly.
GitHub Releases indicate multiple 1.x releases most months in 2024, often spaced days to a week or two apart (i.e., roughly weekly to biweekly on average).
There is no separate named "beta" or "canary" channel on PyPI; the main 1.x stream is the stable distribution. Pre-releases are uncommon and not a separate channel.
The repository/docs show the v1-style client API (e.g., `from openai import OpenAI`), consistent with the 1.x major release line being current.
The project uses semantic versioning with incremental 1.x minor/patch updates rather than parallel stable/LTS tracks.
